subject: LangMate — L10n qualification & eval plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Brun <sophie.brun@langmate.com>, Tomás Alvarez <t.alvarez@langmate.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: LangMate — L10n qualification & eval plan

Hi Sophie / Tomás,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand LangMate's roadmap for language coverage across EU and APAC markets. Quick recap and a pragmatic next-steps proposal so we can validate model fit against your QA criteria without blocking engineering timelines.

Recap (short):
- Primary locales: French (FR), European Spanish (ES-ES), German (DE), Japanese (JA), Korean (KO).
- Primary use-cases: UI copy translation+adaptation, customer support response generation, and short-form marketing localization.
- Constraints: data residency preference for EU, tolerances for hallucination (max 1% critical-content hallucination), tone consistency requirements for brand voice.

Proposed immediate next steps (high priority):
1) Share a small representative eval bundle from your QA team (sample CSV + reference responses) — we can ingest this and run an automated pass.
2) Redwood to push two model profiles for a quick comparison: a compact verified open model for throughput (13B 8-bit) and a high-quality text model (Redwood-mtext-xxl-v1 quantized).
3) Benchmarks: we’ll run our standard multilingual metrics (BLEU/chrF, token-level hallucination checks, and our brand-voice style score).
4) 72-hour smoke run followed by a 30-min sync to review results and decide on a broader eval.

Attachments I’m sending with this message: redwood-multilang-profiles.pdf (model profiles & expected latency/cost) and prompt-set-fr-es-de-ja-ko.xlsx (sample prompts we’ll use).

If that plan sounds good, please reply with a single CSV (<= 1k rows) and we’ll get Connor O’Brien (SE) to provision a secure upload and run the smoke test.

Thanks — I’ll block time on Jan 25 in case you want to review the first pass live.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

--
Attachment stubs: redwood-multilang-profiles.pdf (PDF), prompt-set-fr-es-de-ja-ko.xlsx (XLSX)

Subject: Re: LangMate — L10n qualification & eval plan

Thanks Vanessa — that plan looks useful and pragmatic. Quick clarifications from our side before we share the sample:

- Data residency: for the eval we can provide anonymized test sets but need assurances that any stored outputs for EU data remain in-region (will that be possible for the smoke run?).
- Languages & labels: the CSV will include locale tags (fr-FR, es-ES, de-DE, ja-JP, ko-KR) and reference translations.
- Metrics: we also care about brand-voice drift; do you have a simple rubric you use for that?

I’m attaching a tiny sample (langmate-eval-sample.csv) to validate format. We’ll plan to send a 500–800 row set once you confirm the upload method and residency.

Available to sync Jan 25 morning CET — if the smoke run can be EU-only that would be preferred.

Best,
Sophie Brun
Head of Localization Engineering | LangMate Solutions

Subject: Re: LangMate — L10n qualification & eval plan

Hi Sophie — great, and thanks for the sample. Short answers and what we’ll do next: 

Residency: yes — for the smoke run we can limit compute and storage to our EU region (Frankfurt) under Redwood Private evaluation tenancy. We’ll provide an audit log snapshot you can review after the run.

Brand-voice rubric: we have a lightweight 5-point rubric we apply (accuracy, tone match, brevity, terminology preservation, and hallucination). I’m linking the dashboard in the metadata but also attaching the model profile PDF that describes the expected tradeoffs.

Model recommendations (what we’ll run in the 72-hour smoke):
- Profile A (throughput-focused): open-13b-8bit (fast; expected median latency ~120ms/token; cost-effective for batch support responses).
- Profile B (quality-focused): redwood-mtext-xxl-v1-q4 (higher per-token quality on short-context creative/marketing outputs; higher latency but tighter brand-voice).

Prompt sets: we’ll apply your reference translations as evaluation prompts and our brand-voice scoring prompts from prompt-set-fr-es-de-ja-ko.xlsx. We’ll also run a short adversarial hallucination probe to estimate failure modes.

Next: once Connor provisions the upload link we’ll ingest the sample and run the smoke. Target turn-around: 72 hours from upload. I’ll schedule the Jan 25 sync (CET morning) and send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looping in Connor to close the provisioning steps.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: LangMate — L10n qualification & eval plan (provisioning details)

Hi Sophie, Vanessa — Connor here (SE). I’ll provision the secure EU upload and kick off the smoke run once you drop the full CSV. Quick technical notes and the checklist we’ll follow so everything is auditable: 

1) Upload: I will create a pre-authenticated upload endpoint (EU only) and send temporary credentials that expire after 7 days. Expect a signed S3 URL and an audit token.
2) Ingestion: accepted formats — CSV with columns [id, locale, source_text, reference_text, notes]. You can reuse the sample format.
3) Outputs we’ll produce and share: per-locale BLEU and chrF, brand-voice score (0-5), hallucination rate, token cost and median latency, and an ops log with region/time stamps.
4) Baseline thresholds we’ll call out in the report (initial): BLEU >= 0.45 (for translation-style prompts), chrF >= 0.50, brand-voice >= 3.5, hallucination <= 1.5% critical content. We’ll surface any locale-model pairs that fall outside these bands.
5) Smoke-run window: 72 hours from upload. We’ll keep you updated in the shared dashboard and push a results PDF at the end.

I’ll attach the temporary upload instruction doc (attachment stub) and will open the upload link by EOD CET today.

Connor O’Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
